columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Free E2EE messaging and calls; app and Signal Protocol are open source (Signal Foundation nonprofit).
Co-founded by Moxie Marlinspike; Brian Acton donated ~USD 50M to start the foundation. Operating needs estimated ≈USD 50M/year by 2025 (~USD 14M infrastructure today).
Voice/video outbound bandwidth ~20 petabytes/year (~USD 1.7M/year bandwidth for calls alone).
Tens of millions of users; widely adopted by privacy-conscious individuals, journalists, and activists.

strengths.title: Strong privacy and security guarantees
strengths.detail: E2EE by default; foundation states it has no data to sell, no advertisers, and no shareholders.

strengths.title: Open-source protocol and app
strengths.detail: Public verification of code; Signal Protocol underpins encryption in other major apps as well.

strengths.title: Simple, free, cross-platform UX
strengths.detail: Secure messaging plus voice and video calls; no ads; limited distractions.

strengths.title: Reliable messaging over data
strengths.detail: Often more reliable than SMS, with clear message status and strong media support.

weaknesses.title: Phone-number identity and onboarding friction
weaknesses.detail: Requires phone number registration, harder for full pseudonymity and multi-device flows.

weaknesses.title: Limited social discovery and communities
weaknesses.detail: Great for private groups and 1:1; lacks feeds, discovery, and community management vs Discord or Facebook Groups.

weaknesses.title: Funding and sustainability pressures
weaknesses.detail: Nonprofit model (~USD 50M/year need) depends on donations and grants rather than commercial revenue.

weaknesses.title: Smaller user base vs WhatsApp/Telegram
weaknesses.detail: Harder to reach large communities when not everyone has Signal installed.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Signal is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Signal is a free, open-source, end-to-end encrypted messaging app for private messaging and calls, developed by the nonprofit Signal Foundation with no ads and no data to sell.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Signal side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Signal you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Signal

You can use both. Signal keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Signal. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
